## (b) How the model gets API knowledge

- System prompt per version is byte-stable for cache: hard rules + modbuilder.json spec + `knowledge(mcVersion)` appended (prompts.js:35-58 area). `PROMPT_VERSION = "mb-2026-10-09.1"` (prompts.js:10).
- **Sheets**: `services/modbuilder/sheets/<ver>.md`, 4 files (1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11), each ~15 KB, 42 bullet facts in the 1.21.11 file; **the whole sheet for the requested version is injected on every build** (prompts.js `sheetFor`, not retrieval). Generated once by `sheets/gen-sheets.py` (hand-written template with version branches, claims "checked with javap" against the Paper jar). They are the source of truth after generation; regen
- **Rules**: `rules/failure-rules.json` (12 KB; 18 rules: 12 for `*`, 3 for 1.21.4-1.21.11, 1 for 1.21.1, 1 for 1.21.11, 1 for 1.21.8-1.21.11); mined with `tools/mine-rules.py`. Injected as "LESSONS FROM EARLIER FAILED BUILDS".
- Note: `GameSupport.knowledge` / `KnowledgePack` (lib/cyrus/games/support.ts:55-60) describes a retrieval design ("retrieval injects only the lines for the APIs a plan touches") but the Minecraft build service does not use it; that path belongs to Valheim/Terraria knowledge files (lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts). Two knowledge systems.
- Size: sheet + rules is roughly 4-5k tokens per build (UNVERIFIED estimate from 15 KB).

## (c) Where the new pieces plug in

1. **ModSpec / project model**: new typed JSON stored per project. Natural home: a new table keyed by `rootBuildId` (same convention as `CyrusModPage.rootBuildId @unique`, schema.prisma:9171) and a per-revision snapshot, not more fields in `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON (that column is already overloaded: per-build model/attachments + per-project title/listing, meta.ts:16-33). Revision identity today = `ModBuild.id`; so "revision" should reference `ModBui
2. **Build request**: `POST /builds` body and `lib/modbuilder/create.ts:30-115` (builds the service payload; `attachmentIds` -> `images`). Add `spec` and `assets` here; service side `server.js:866` handler and `initialPrompt/changePrompt` (prompts.js:77-100) to pass the spec as a file in the workspace (e.g. `spec.json`, allowed write area is `src/main/**` + `modbuilder.json`, prompts.js rule 2).
3. **Workspace/packaging**: resources already land in the jar from `src/main/resources/**` (jar built from javac output dir, server.js:521, UNVERIFIED whether resources are copied into `out/` before `jar`; see server.js ~518 "Resources (plugin.yml, config.yml, ...)"). A resource pack must be a SEPARATE zip artifact (alongside `artifact.jar`, `jarPath` in `ModBuild`, schema.prisma `jarPath/jarSha256`). `ModBuild` has no pack columns; stored jars a
4. **Install**: `lib/mods/installers/minecraft.ts` `place()` returns `PlacedFile[]` of arbitrary paths (types.ts), so the engine can already write extra files with backup/rollback; `resolveCyrus` (installers/cyrus.ts:45) returns the jar via `loadCyrusJar` (cyrus-mods/registry.ts:54). Add a second package (pack zip) there.
5. **DB**: new tables (see 1), and `GameMod`/`ServerMod` already model per-server installs (schema.prisma:3610).
6. **NxLabs generator**: `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts:170 buildModDoc(chain)` creates the page doc from builds; add an "assets" section sourced from the spec; `CyrusModMedia`/`ModMedia` exist for images (schema.prisma:3800, 9342).
7. **Studio UI state**: client store keeps a studio-side `Mod`/`ModVersion` model (lib/cyrus/types.ts, real.ts maps ModBuild -> Mod, real.ts:1-14); files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`.

## (d) Can the Mods engine deliver a resource pack and set server.properties on a customer's itzg server?

- Layout: Minecraft servers are itzg/minecraft-server in a Docker container named `mc` on a customer VM; `/opt/mc` on the VM = container `/data`; env in `/root/mc.env`; run flags `-v /opt/mc:/data --env-file /root/mc.env` (worker/game-config.ts:782, installers/minecraft.ts header). Files are reached over SSH (`SshGuestFs`, lib/modbuilder/install.ts:56-61; lib/mods/guest-fs.ts).
- **Placing a pack file**: yes, mechanically (PlacedFile path under `/opt/mc`), but a Minecraft `resource-pack` setting needs an **HTTP(S) URL** and SHA-1; a local file on the server is not served (no web server in the container). So the pack zip must be hosted by Nxeon (the NX Labs mirror exists, installers/cyrus.ts doc comment; `lib/mods/mirror.ts`; UNVERIFIED that it serves arbitrary public URLs).
- **Setting server.properties**: possible. `applyMinecraft` finds `server.properties`, rewrites keys with `updateKeyValue` via SFTP (worker/game-config.ts:793-826). But **no resource-pack field exists** in the game-config schema (grep for `resource-pack|RESOURCE_PACK` returned nothing in lib/ or worker/ apart from unrelated "Resource Packs" category labels: lib/mods-browse.ts:99, installers/minecraft.ts:51-55 which actively marks resource packs "
- The engine has no "post-install config step" hook, no uninstall of properties (engine uninstall removes files it placed, engine.ts:442), and `restartRequired: true` (installers/minecraft.ts:~495). Needed: a typed "server settings patch" operation recorded in the state file so uninstall can revert it.
- Alternative: Paper plugin generated by Cyrus calling `Player#setResourcePack(url, sha1bytes, prompt, force)` on join (needs no server.properties change; uses the plugin path that already works). Also requires the URL to be reachable. Note the safety scan forbids networking for the plugin itself (rules/net-policy.json, prompts rule 5), but setResourcePack only hands a URL to the client (UNVERIFIED whether scan.js flags it).

## (e) What `textures/` and `sfx.ts` actually do

- `lib/cyrus/textures/*` (7 files, ~350 lines): `dsl.ts` = declarative `TextureSpec` (16/32/64 px, palette, <=400 ops: fill/px/rect/line/circle/poly/gradient/noise/shade/outline); `render.ts` = deterministic RGBA rasteriser; `png.ts` encoder; `zip.ts`; `pack.ts` `buildPack()` = 1-24 **item** textures -> `assets/<ns>/{textures/item,models/item,items}/<name>` (1.21.4+ `items/` model definitions for `setItemModel`) + pack.mcmeta + sha1. Nothing else
- `lib/cyrus/sfx.ts` (155 lines): **UI feedback sounds** synthesised in the browser with Web Audio (tick, ping, whoosh, stage, success, error, thump), off by default, `localStorage "cyrus-sfx"`; imported only by `lib/cyrus/fx.ts:12` and `CyrusDemo.tsx:26`. It cannot produce game sound effects and writes no files. So "Sound Studio" has no code beyond this; the owner's 514-MP3 library is not referenced anywhere in code (no grep hits needed; UNVERIF
- Studio copy still says coming soon (`components/cyrus/marketing/StudioArt.tsx` matched the "coming soon" grep).

## (f) Plan-tier reading and where to gate asset features

- `TOKEN_TIERS = free|katara|saka|all` (lib/cyrus/tokens/config.ts:10), `PLAN_TIERS` without free (:12). Effective tier: `effectiveTier({plan, override, ...})` (tokens/economy.ts:44-59; handles active/trialing/past_due/canceled windows and admin override); loader `tierOf(userId)` (tokens/access.ts:37). Tier -> allowed models only: `TIER_MODELS` (economy.ts:15-20), `canUseModel` (:25).
- Single enforcement point for builds: `gateBuild` (tokens/builds.ts:25-50), called once from `lib/modbuilder/create.ts:72`. It is only active when `tokensActiveFor` (live flag or preview list, access.ts:18-27); otherwise builds pass through untracked.
- Gate asset features there: extend `gateBuild`'s input with requested asset features and return a new `code` (e.g. `asset_locked`), and read the tier via `tierOf` for UI (`buildTokenState`, tokens/state.ts:13-26). Model names (katara/saka/yakko) double as tier names in the UI and in `engine/kit.ts:365 MODEL_NAME`; do not conflate with feature tiers. No feature-flag table keyed by tier exists (UNVERIFIED beyond grep of tierOf/canUseModel usage).
- Note: NxLabs publication has its own gate (lib/cyrus/public-gate.ts, lib/cyrus-mods/gate.ts); asset licensing checks (owner's SFX licence) should go there.

## (g) Ranked missing pieces / debt that will hurt scaling

1. **No project/spec/asset data model** and `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON overloaded; revisions are build rows with no diff/rollback of assets (schema.prisma:8590; meta.ts). Blocks everything below.
2. **Version support is hardcoded in 4+ places** and tied to JDK 21/`--release 21`/Gradle template toolchain 21 (types.ts:3, Dockerfile:11,49, server.js:513, template/build.gradle.kts:21-25). 26.x cannot be added without a registry + JDK 25 (E-versions.md).
3. **Knowledge = whole-sheet injection per version, hand-generated, no 26.x**; two incompatible knowledge systems (`KnowledgePack` retrieval vs services sheets). Sheets will not scale to creatures/models/GUI/particles/datapack APIs; token cost per build rises with every addition.
4. **Asset pipeline missing end-to-end**: textures only items, unwired; no model/entity/animation/sound generation; no sounds.json; sfx.ts is UI-only; pack format table wrong for 26.x.
5. **Delivery path for client assets missing**: no resource-pack URL hosting, no `resource-pack`/sha1 config field, no pack artifact in `ModBuild`, engine has no settings-patch step; installer marks resource packs unsupported (installers/minecraft.ts:55).
6. **Plugin-only ceiling**: Paper-plugin sandbox (no reflection/NMS/networking rules) cannot express custom mobs with custom models, blocks, dimensions without datapacks/resource packs; datapack placement exists in the installer (installers/minecraft.ts:455-465) but the generator never produces datapacks (UNVERIFIED but no code does).
7. **No mod-vs-mod conflict engine or mod packs**: engine handles file ownership only (engine.ts:281); no pack/bundle entity.
8. **No import-your-own-mod flow** (no code, no scanner path for foreign jars; scan.js works on freshly compiled bytecode in the workspace).
9. **Eval coverage thin**: 30 prompts (13 runtime-loaded) on 1.21.x only; rtcheck uses `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`, mineflayer bot, per-version Paper jars on the build VM (eval/rtcheck.py:1-15); no assets, no multi-version matrix, ops live on a single VM (`/root/...` paths, run_eval.py reads `/root/modbuilder.env`).
10. **Simulated template engine (1701 lines) alongside the real path** — risk of divergence and confusion for non-Minecraft games (lib/cyrus/engine/templates.ts).
11. **Single build VM**: concurrency 2, 20 min timeout, `/data` on one host (server.js:44-60); no queue/scale-out story (UNVERIFIED beyond defaults).
12. **Tier model conflation**: plans gate models, not features; `gateBuild` only tracks when economy is live.

## Could not determine
Whether `jar` includes `src/main/resources/**` via an explicit copy (read only lines ~511-521, ~518 comment); the NX Labs mirror's ability to host public pack URLs; whether scan.js flags `setResourcePack`; itzg env/file precedence; any use of the 514-MP3 library in code (not searched beyond the Cyrus dirs).

- Scheduling: sync runTask-family 60%, Bukkit async 43%, ExecutorService 36%, CompletableFuture 32%, extends BukkitRunnable 26%, legacy scheduleSync* 24%, Folia region schedulers 42%.
- Persistence: NIO files 64%, YAML 62%, Gson JSON 53%, JDBC 37% (Hikari 5%, SQLite/MySQL/H2 each under 2% as direct refs), PDC 34%, Java serialization 22%, none 12%.
- Config: config.yml in 47%; median 47 keys, 8 top-level, depth 3; 85% commented; top keys debug, language, enabled, database, messages, storage.
- Commands: 53% declare commands (median 1); 58% have aliases; 39% set a permission field; permission nodes start with the plugin name 90%; depth 3 most common; frequent suffixes `*`, others, reload, admin, use, bypass.
- Deps: any depend/softdepend 64%; softdepend PlaceholderAPI 62, Vault 38, WorldGuard 27, LuckPerms 23, ProtocolLib 17, ViaVersion 14, floodgate 14.
- Telemetry/network: bStats 58%, update checker (modrinth/spiget/github) 28%, http/socket classes 64%. Reflection 66%, NMS/CraftBukkit 23%, Brigadier/Lifecycle commands 24%, paper-plugin.yml 10%, `libraries:` 10%, shading other packages 51%, Kotlin 2%.

## Top gaps vs Cyrus (sheets, prompts.js, rules, minecraft.ts, designer; word-match, 146/300 popular API classes mentioned)
1. Events used by 10-20% of plugins and absent from Cyrus text: PlayerChangedWorld, PluginDisable, PlayerCommandPreprocess, InventoryOpen, WorldLoad/Unload, ChunkLoad/Unload, Block Piston Extend/Retract, PlayerSwapHandItems, CreatureSpawn (+SpawnReason), PlayerFish, EntityShootBow, ProjectileLaunch, FoodLevelChange, SignChange, PlayerLogin/AsyncPlayerPreLogin, AsyncTabComplete.
2. APIs unmentioned: OfflinePlayer (49% of plugins), BlockFace, BlockState/BlockStateMeta, Chunk, SkullMeta, PotionMeta, BookMeta, DyeColor, Biome, Villager/merchant, ExperienceOrb, FixedMetadataValue (metadata), ServicesManager, Bukkit BossBar (BarColor/Style/Flag; Cyrus teaches only Adventure), InventoryType/InventoryView, PermissionDefault, ConsoleCommandSender, Bukkit.getConsoleSender, NamespacedKey.fromString, Block.getRelative/setType/getBlockData, isPrimaryThread.
3. Pattern conflicts (real plugins do it; Cyrus forbids or never mentions): networking, reflection/Class.forName (62%), NMS, Brigadier, Folia schedulers, bStats, shading, Vault/PlaceholderAPI/WorldGuard softdepends (no lane for new plugins), JSON/SQL storage (Cyrus teaches YAML only), legacy ChatColor.translateAlternateColorCodes (still 31%).
4. Datapacks: dialog, predicate (23%), item_modifier (18%), damage_type, worldgen structure/template_pool/processor_list (23%) and `execute`-heavy functions (66k `execute` vs 17k `scoreboard` lines) sit outside the spec; Cobblemon-style species/spawn packs skew the sample.
5. Archetypes with ~0 keyword hits in Cyrus text and eval: minigame arena/lobby/queue, party/guild/clan, moderation/punishments, region claims/protection, backpack/storage, machines/automation, custom blocks/furniture, entity-limit/lag tools, voice/proxy messaging.
Resource packs: models 42%, item/block textures ~40%, optifine CIT 30%, gui 26%, lang 19%, core shaders 9%, fonts 9%, custom sounds 5%; median zip 0.3 MB; none use custom_model_data files (the 1.21.4+ item-model path is the norm).

## Recommendations
- API sheets: add an events catalog (the ~20 above, cancel/async semantics), a block/world sheet (BlockFace, BlockState, Chunk), head/potion/book metas, OfflinePlayer (warn: name lookup is blocking), Bukkit BossBar equivalence, metadata API.
- Failure rules (precheck): Bukkit.getOfflinePlayer(String) on main thread, Player.spigot(), translateAlternateColorCodes, Class.forName, PlayerMove without hasChangedBlock, async Bukkit calls.
- Templates: Gson JSON per-UUID store (Gson is on the classpath), PDC item tags, listener skeletons for the top 10 events.
- Coverage matrix: add rows weighted by category counts above (minigame, social, management, storage, technology, decoration).
- Eval set: one prompt per new event and per missing archetype, plus 1.21.1 enum-era variants; keep refusal cases for network/reflection/NMS.

## Not fetched / caveats
- Skipped >60 MB: puffradio (131 MB), cobblemon-music-pack (342 MB), cobblemon mod (139 MB).
- Plugin/resourcepack sets are smaller than the nominal quota (173, 43) because per-category tops overlap the overall tops; the `features`/`resolutions` resource-pack headers were not treated as categories.
- Top-by-downloads is skewed to big multi-platform projects (Simple Voice Chat, WorldEdit); several client-only mods leaked into other-loader (server_side optional). No compile check (no source). Relocated shaded libs inside the plugin package count as own code.

# BL: Recipe memory ("learned paths") design (2026-10-12)

Short design. Context: `BL-token-savings-plan.md` (lever L2, backlog B6/B7), `BK-learning-loop.md` (signals, anonymized export, mining), `BF-mc-technique-catalogue.md` (seed material). V = verified in code/data, U = estimate.

## 1. What it is, in one paragraph

A **recipe** is a small, verified, generic implementation pattern for one mechanic (for example "per-player home store with permission-based limit and safe async teleport"), written by us. At plan time Cyrus picks the matching recipe with a cheap lookup and injects only that recipe into the build's first user turn. A **path memory** table records, per archetype, which lane / tier / effort / recipe actually worked and what it cost, learned from anonymized outcomes, and feeds the plan-screen estimate and the router. Neither one ever contains or is derived from a user's code, an imported mod, or 

## 2. Recipe schema (JSON next to the build service, like `rules/failure-rules.json`)

```
services/modbuilder/recipes/<id>.json
{
  "id": "homes-store",
  "version": 3,                       // part of knowledgeVersion() and the dedupe key
  "archetypes": ["homes", "warps"],   // ids from lib/cyrus/adapters/minecraft-coverage.json
  "lanes": ["plugin", "config"],
  "mcVersions": ["1.21.1","1.21.4","1.21.8","1.21.11"],
  "title": "...", "summary": "<= 3 sentences, what the mechanic is",
  "pattern": "<= 600 tokens of prose + at most 40 lines of skeleton, only for the tricky parts",
  "configSchema": [{key, type, default, min, max, why}],   // the keys a mod of this kind should expose
  "paperFacts": ["World#getChunkAtAsync", "Entity#teleportAsync"],  // javap-checked per version
  "pitfalls": [{"ruleId": "ondisable-sync-save", "note": "..."}],   // links to failure-rules.json + BF gotchas
  "boundedWork": "<how NxPerf budgets apply, or 'none'>",
  "tests": "golden/plugins/mc-homes/golden.json",                     // RCON expectations, already exist for 54 archetypes
  "provenance": {"author": "nxeon", "sources": ["BF:plg-safe-teleport-async","golden:mc-homes","rule:ondisable-sync-save"],
                 "noUserCode": true, "noReferenceCorpusCode": true, "reviewedBy": "...", "reviewedAt": "2026-10-.."},
  "stats": {"n": 0, "withRecipe": {...}, "without": {...}},          // filled by the eval, not by hand
  "status": "draft|verified|retired"
}
```

Seed set (all ours): the 33 BF `plugin` techniques with `gotchas` and effort S (safe teleport, teleport warmup/cooldown, config snapshot reload, chest-GUI anti-dupe, ondisable sync save, async chat renderer, playermove filter, hologram text display, per-player FX with reconcile), the bounded-work pattern from NxPerf (perf rule 10), the 54 golden plugins that already map to archetypes (V: 54 of the 63 plain archetypes have a golden), and the 33 failure rules. A recipe is the *explanation + skeleton* of a golden, not a copy of any third-party plugin. Start with 8-12; add by demand from the minin

## 3. Selection at plan time (no extra model call)

1. **Free:** the existing intake guard (Haiku, 1 turn, already run on every build, replaces the classifier, V `route.js`) also returns up to 2 archetype ids from the closed list of 85 (about +10 output tokens). Prompt change in `GUARD_PROMPT`/`parseGuard`; unknown ids are dropped.
2. **Fallback / cross-check:** a deterministic scorer over the same 85 rows (label, category, technique words, template tags; there is already a keyword rule set in `lib/cyrus/planner/rules.ts` and a trigram helper `lib/cyrus/prompt-trigrams.ts`). If the guard's id and the scorer agree, confidence high; if only one fires, inject only when the recipe `status` is verified and the match score passes a threshold; otherwise inject nothing. A wrong recipe is worse than none.
3. **Never** inject for: change builds without a mapped archetype, imported mods, refused requests. For a change build, use the base build's recorded recipe id (anonymous metadata we store ourselves), not a fresh match.
4. Result is recorded on the build (`recipeId`, `recipeVersion`, `matchSource`) so the cost effect is measurable.

## 4. Injection (cache-safe, small)

Goes into the first user turn next to `planBlock()` (V: `prompts.js`), NOT the system prompt, so the cached base prefix stays byte-identical:

```
TESTED PATTERN for this kind of mod (follow it unless the request needs something else): <title>
<pattern prose + skeleton> / Settings to expose: ... / Known pitfalls: ...
```

Cost model (U): 600-900 tokens injected = about $0.005-0.008 on Sonnet (one cache write plus ~9 reads); it pays for itself if it removes 700 output tokens of design thinking or one repair turn ($0.010-0.04). Budget cap: 900 tokens per recipe, one recipe per build (two only if they share no pitfalls).

## 5. Path memory (archetype -> best path -> expected cost)

Table built weekly by the learning job (B7), from `BuildSignals` (rework, regression, outcome, cost, turns, effort, model, recipe id, repairs, autofix ids, failure-rule ids):

```
key: (archetypeSet, laneSet, tier, fresh|change)
value: { n, successRate, keptRate, costUsd {p25,p50,p90}, turns p50, repairs p50,
         bestEffort, bestRecipeId, recipeEffect {ratio, ci, n}, lastUpdated }
```

Rules: a cell is shown or used only with n >= 8 (shrink toward the prior `BASE` table below that); "best" = highest keptRate among options with n >= 5, ties by lower p50 cost; a path with one rework in the last 5 is demoted. Used for: (a) plan-screen estimate (typical / up to), (b) default effort and tier suggestion for that archetype (suggestion only, the customer still picks the tier), (c) recipe A/B bookkeeping (`recipeEffect`), (d) the admin Learning tab. It changes nothing automatically: new defaults ship as engine releases through `release-manifest.ts` with an eval gate (BK).

## 6. Learning from outcomes (and what is never learned)

Learned (anonymized, default on, no request text): archetype ids, lanes, tier, model, effort, recipe id, turns, cost, success / kept / rework / regression flags, repair count, **normalized failure signatures** (javac error class plus the Paper API symbol only when it appears in the version's API index; rule ids; autofix ids), and which repair resolved which signature.
Mined into **candidates** (never auto-applied, same as BK): `recipe-pitfall` (signature X recurred in 3+ builds of archetype A without a rule -> propose a pitfall line or failure rule), `path-stat` (a lane/effort combination beats the default), `recipe-gap` (archetype with no recipe and p50 cost above its tier's median -> author one).
Never learned: any user text, class or command names, config contents, code, imported mods, Modrinth corpus code. Recipes are authored and reviewed by us from our own goldens, BF technique ids and javap facts; the mining job only changes *which* of our recipes is chosen and *which pitfall we add*, never the content from a user's work. Template sharing of a user's mod is separate and opt-in (D-60 / D-61 wording).

## 7. Gates before any recipe ships

1. `tools/recipes/lint.ts`: schema, provenance present, every `paperFacts` symbol exists in all listed version jars (javap, as `gen-sheets.py` does), every `pitfalls.ruleId` exists.
2. **Similarity gate:** 8-gram shingle overlap of pattern + skeleton against (a) the private reference corpus index (`/tank/cyrus-library-staging/_reference-mods`, private, offline only) and (b) every stored user build source: must be about 0; a hit blocks the recipe.
3. Golden test: the linked `golden.json` flies green on all four versions.
4. Eval: 2 runs of the archetype's coverage prompts with and without the recipe (about $0.3 per archetype per run on Sonnet 5.5). Ship only if success and first-try are not lower, runtime checks pass, and cost per success is lower or equal (record `recipeEffect`).
5. Rollback: flag `CYRUS_RECIPES` / `MB_RECIPES` off = prompt byte-identical to today (tested).

## 8. Plan-screen implications

- Estimate = path-memory cell (typical / likely max, sample size) x measured `recipeEffect` only when n >= 8; otherwise the plain number plus a badge "tested pattern: usually fewer fixes", no discount. After Saka -> 5.5 and effort routing the cells reset, so `stats` must record the engine release.
- A recipe is a chip the user can see and turn off ("Using the tested Homes pattern"), because it can change the result's shape; off = free-form build and the estimate reverts.
- Identical template-chip prompts can offer the **starter bank** line instead (instant, about 5 tokens), which is the zero-model end of the same idea.

## 9. Rollout

B6 seed 8 recipes + guard archetype ids + injection behind flags (owner/preview accounts first); B1/B7 capture and path memory run in parallel (read-only); eval per recipe; widen to the 54 goldens by mined demand; later NxKit (backlog B9) so recipes call tested helpers instead of carrying skeletons. Expected effect (U): 15-35% per hit build, hit rate 35-55% of plain builds, so 5-19% of spend; the owner's own 13 root prompts would have hit a recipe 3-6 times.

# BL: Cyrus token-savings plan (2026-10-12)

Owner goal: if a simple mod costs people too many tokens, Cyrus is not worth it. This note finds every place tokens or compute are spent, measures what can be measured, and ranks the ways to cut spend without making mods worse. It extends BJ (token baseline) and BK (learning loop); BJ's levers are listed in the ranking by number but not re-analysed. Companion: `BL-recipe-memory-design.md`.

Labels: **V** = verified in code (cyrus-rc2) or in read-only SELECTs of the production `ModBuild` table / decompiled jars of the 25 stored builds. **U** = estimate or judgment, with the assumption stated. No build was run, nothing was written anywhere except these two files.

**Sample warning (V):** production holds 28 builds, ALL from the owner (1 distinct user), $7.33 total. Nothing here is a forecast for public traffic. The numbers rank where to look and what to measure.

---

## 0. The five findings that matter

1. **Where the money is (V + U).** Code the model writes is only about 25-40% of a build's cost (U). The rest is thinking before the first edit (planning = 51% of wall time, BJ; the owner saw 3.5-4 min on a 700-word spec), one API round trip per file on Sonnet 5, and cold prompt-cache writes. Shrinking prompts, sheets or boilerplate is therefore worth single digits; model choice, effort, turn count and rework are worth tens of percent.
2. **The Saka tier is on Sonnet 5, not 5.5 (V).** All 11 Saka (non-guard) calls in the data resolved to `claude-sonnet-5` (`MB_TIER_SAKA` default). A fresh Saka build: median $0.55 (range $0.22-0.83), 9-10 turns, 450 s. The 0.3 eval measured Sonnet 5.5 at 2-3 requests and 49% cheaper. This is the largest single lever (BJ #1) and needs no code.
3. **The plan screen under-states cost (V).** I ran the real `estimate()` over the 25 successful builds: **20 exceeded the top of the shown range**, 3 were inside, 2 under. Median actual / shown-high: Saka fresh 2.4x, Saka change 2.5x, Katara change 2.1x, Katara fresh 1.0x, Yakko 1.2x. Users are charged actual cost (not capped at the hold), so the plan screen is the biggest "silently more expensive than shown" problem. See section 3.
4. **Owner's pre-made-structures idea: real but modest on tokens (V shares, U savings).** Of the code the model writes, about 26% is scaffoldable boilerplate (section 4), which is 4-10% of a plain build's cost. Its bigger value is removing failure classes (plugin.yml/getCommand mismatch, unsaved data, reload) and feeding recipes. Typed specs that compile to Java (designer lanes) save far more per hit (70-90% of code tokens) but only 18 of 85 archetypes use them today.
5. **Two things that look like savings are traps (V).** `MB_DEDUPE=on` is cross-user (the key has no user id): it would hand one customer another customer's source, which breaks the owner's "never reproduce a user's mod" rule. And "refunds for guard refusals" only release the hold: `cyrus_tok_charge_refused` defaults to true, so a refused or falsely refused request still costs the 5-token floor.

---

## 1. Where the tokens go (measured, 28 builds)

Spend by call kind from `result.ai.calls` (V):

| kind | calls | turns | spend | share | $/turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| change | 13 | 221 | $3.24 | 44% | 0.015 |
| generate | 10 | 62 | $2.93 | 40% | 0.047 |
| repair | 7 | 22 | $0.22 | 3% | 0.010 |
| repair-asset | 2 | 5 | $0.22 | 3% | 0.043 |
| guard | 19 | 19 | $0.08 | 1% | 0.004 |
| (builds before AI records) | | | $0.64 | 9% | |

By model resolved: Haiku 4.5 (Katara) 19 guard + 19 gen/change/repair calls; **Sonnet 5** (Saka) 11 calls, $4.00 (55% of spend); Opus 5 (Yakko) 2 calls, $1.09. Fresh median cost by tier: Katara $0.092, Saka $0.55, Yakko $0.55 (n=2). Opus fresh builds (6-7 turns, $0.41 / $0.69) were NOT dearer than Sonnet 5 fresh builds (9-10 turns, $0.22-0.83): Sonnet 5's turn count eats its price advantage.

Cost anatomy of a typical build (U, from the 0.5 efficiency analysis on the eval mods, `cyrus-v6/efficiency/EFFICIENCY.md`, scaled): output tokens 61% (of which 40-77% is thinking depending on model), cache writes 33% (everything generated is written back to the cache at the 1 h TTL price, 2x input), cache reads 6%. On the owner's heavier prompts the thinking share is higher: a 475 s Sonnet 5 build (ChunkDup, 10 turns, $0.82) wrote about 5.6k tokens of Java (decompiled estimate) plus about 1k of

| 4 | Fresh generation | Katara Haiku / Saka Sonnet 5 / Yakko Opus 5 | 4-10 turns | Haiku $0.04-0.15; Sonnet 5 $0.22-0.83; Opus $0.41-0.69 | user | estimate below (too low) |
| 5 | Change build | same model as base | 12-31 turns (reads workspace + edits) | Haiku $0.08-0.27; Sonnet 5 $0.28-0.65 | user | `CHANGE_COST_FACTOR 0.8` (measured 1.7x for Katara) |
| 6 | Cheap first repair (small compile error) | Haiku via `--resume` | 1-7 turns | $0.004-0.04 | user | **not active on tier builds**: `rec.override` set, so repairs stay on the generate model (V: `server.js` repair ladder) |
| 7 | Model repair / escalation (after 2 failed repairs, one tier up, no notice) | Sonnet/Opus | up to 25 turns | Sonnet 5 repair $0.10; repair-asset $0.034-0.18 | user (charged at the build's own multiplier) | not in estimate |

### Silently paid by the user (flag these)

1. **Cold-cache prefix writes and thinking** (rows 9-10): the biggest terms, not visible, not in the estimate.
2. **Repairs and asset repairs on a SUCCESSFUL build** (rows 6-8): fully charged (the failure-credit rule `cyrus_tok_free_failures=3` per 7 days applies to FAILED builds only; over the limit failures are charged in full). The 10-12 Spawner-Wand build spent 33% of its $0.65 on two asset-repair rounds.
3. **Escalation** (row 7): a Katara build can be finished by Sonnet or Opus without telling the user.
4. **The guard** (row 2): charged even when it refuses, including false refusals (the 10-12 06:52 ChunkMirror refusal charged 5 tokens, 215 returned). `cyrus_tok_charge_refused` is a Setting.
5. **Charge is not capped at the hold** (`settleCharge` charges full `costUsd`; the ledger only caps at the balance). With estimates 2.4x low, most builds end "over held". The UI shows it, but the user never agreed to it.
6. **Rework** (BJ: 23% of spend re-requested within 30 min), a share of which is the product's fault (planner turned "mob spawner" into a Spawner Wand and replaced the plugin).
7. **Per-build worst case**: `MB_BUILD_BUDGET_USD=4` and `MB_CALL_BUDGET_USD=2.5` default; the largest observed build is $0.83. A runaway loop could charge 2,000 tokens (40% of a daily cap of 5,000) before it stops.

Not charged to users: planner, coach, Test Flight, javac/scan compute, learning jobs, evals.

---

## 3. Plan screen: honesty about "estimated tokens"

Today (V): `estimate()` = 3 buckets x model `costFactor` (katara 0.5, saka 1, yakko 2.5) x lane weights; anchored on Phase 0 Sonnet 5 / small eval prompts. Real data (shown range = `estimate()` for the stored text, no lane weight):

| group | n | actual median | actual range | shown high (median) | actual / high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Katara fresh | 6 | $0.092 (46 tok) | 0.038-0.146 | $0.09 | 1.0x |
| Katara change | 7 | $0.159 (80 tok) | 0.082-0.265 | $0.07 | 2.1x |
| Saka fresh (Sonnet 5) | 4 | $0.55 (275 tok) | 0.217-0.825 | $0.18 | 2.4x |
| Saka change (Sonnet 5) | 6 | $0.435 (218 tok) | 0.055-0.648 | $0.14 | 2.5x |
| Yakko fresh | 2 | $0.547 (274 tok) | 0.407-0.688 | $0.45 | 1.2x |

(tokens at 500 per USD.) Also: a change is not 0.8x a fresh build for Katara (1.7x measured; Haiku explores more), but is for Saka (0.8x).

What honest looks like:
- Show **typical and likely-maximum**, from measured medians and p90 by (tier x fresh/change x lane set), with the sample size behind them when small. Until a cell has n >= 8 builds, show the prior but widen it by the measured correction above and say "early estimate". `Setting cyrus_est_table` (new) so it can be corrected without a deploy.
- State the rule in plain words: "You pay what the build actually uses. We hold up to X; the rest is returned." If the owner wants a hard promise, cap the charge at the hold (Nxeon absorbs the overshoot) until estimates are calibrated: owner decision.
- Say what changes the number: tier, edit vs new, each asset lane (lane weights are guesses, 0.05-0.45), sound library, reference images.
- A **recipe hit** (BL-recipe-memory-design) changes the estimate only by a *measured* effect: `typical x recipeEffect[archetype]` where recipeEffect is the median cost ratio from A/B builds, shown only with n >= 8; before that show a badge ("tested pattern: usually fewer fixes") and no discount. Never show a lower number we have not measured.
- A **starter-bank hit** (ready-made build of a template chip, section 5 L4) is a different line item: "Ready-made, instant, ~5 tokens", exact because there is no model call.
- During the build, the live meter exists (V); add a soft stop at 100% of the hold ("This one is bigger than expected: continue / stop with what you have") so the user, not the service budget, decides.

| knob | where | value | effect | risk | do it when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MB_TIER_SAKA` | service env | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | L0: -35..55% on Saka | medium: eval first | after the $3 v6 eval; reversible by unsetting |

| `cyrus_tok_charge_refused` | admin Setting | `false` | a refused or falsely refused request costs 0 tokens (guard cost $0.0015 absorbed); abuse is bounded by the rate limit (3/min, 20/h) | low | now |
| `cyrus_tok_free_failures` / `_days` | admin Setting | 10 / 7 | failures on our side stay free for longer before "failed_over_limit" charges full | low | now |

Generated 2026-10-12T07:18:05.480Z. Source: ModBuild table, read-only SELECT. Read-only; no prompt, sheet, route or flag was changed. 27 builds, 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-12, total spend $6.51 (about 3,253 Cyrus tokens at $0.002).

**Read this first.** The sample is small (27 builds, all from the owner) and the stored records have cost and turns per AI call but **no token counts**. Savings below are ESTIMATES with stated assumptions; the ranking is for deciding what to measure and try next, not a forecast.

## Headline

- 24/27 builds succeeded; 18 were "kept" successes (not followed by another change within 30 min and not a major regression). Cost per success $0.271; cost per kept success $0.362.
- **Wasted spend**: $1.47 (23% of all spend) went on 4 build(s) the owner followed with another change within 30 minutes; $1.30 on builds that dropped commands or most classes of the build they changed; $0.0080 on failed builds.

| change | 13 | 221 | $3.243 | 50% | $0.0147 |
| generate | 9 | 52 | $2.109 | 32% | $0.0406 |
| repair | 7 | 22 | $0.222 | 3% | $0.0101 |

# Cyrus game onboarding playbook

Playbook version: **1.1.0** (2026-10-11). Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Lessons: [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md).
Owner brief 2026-10-11: onboarding a new game must be flawless and repeatable, and this document keeps improving.
Minecraft is the reference implementation. Hytale and FiveM/RedM are ON HOLD and appear only as worked case studies
([CASE-STUDIES.md](CASE-STUDIES.md)).

This is a living document. It changes only through the loop in [How this playbook stays current](#how-this-playbook-stays-current).

## Start here

```
npx tsx scripts/cyrus/new-game.ts <gameId> --name "Game Name" [--language Lua] [--engine unity]
```
The scaffolder writes the skeleton (adapter at maturity `planned`, GameSupport stub, empty knowledge pack, eval-set
stub, onboarding record, checklist and doc stubs) and **registers nothing**: no adapter in `ADAPTERS`, no catalog row,
no flag. It is idempotent (an existing file is never overwritten). `--docs-only` writes only
`docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (use it for screening, before anyone writes code). `--manifest` prints the derived
capability manifest. Then work through `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` phase by phase (generated from
[templates/TODO.md](templates/TODO.md)).

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/record.json` | phase, status, declared maturity, **evidence**, emitters, owner gate signatures, research reused |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` | the checklist (parsed by `lib/cyrus/onboarding/todo.ts`, shown on `/admin/cyrus/games`) |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/*.md` | the filled templates: SCORECARD, RESEARCH, CAPABILITY, ADAPTER, ASSETS, LEGAL, VERIFICATION, LAUNCH |
| `lib/cyrus/onboarding/` | types (phases, gates, ladder), `health.ts` (ladder exit criteria + record checks), `manifest.ts` (derived capability manifest), `todo.ts`, `records.server.ts` |
| `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` | onboarding health over every record, docs coverage, scaffolder end to end |
| `templates/` | the templates the scaffolder copies, and `templates/agent-briefs/` |

## Principles (non-negotiable)
1. **Delivery first.** A game fits Cyrus only if what we build reaches players without each player installing it by
   hand, or the product is honest that it is a download (research H: "a delivery problem first").
2. **Evidence over claims.** A maturity, a pass rate, a "supported" exists only if it ran and is recorded with a date.
   The onboarding health test fails a record that claims more than its evidence.
3. **Reuse before research.** Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` and the case studies first. Never pay twice for
   the same page. Then read the [skills inventory](skills/README.md) (engine route playbooks and a 74-game field-note
   knowledge base) and grep it for the game and engine. Every record lists the research it reused.
4. **Honest unknowns.** Every fact is labelled V / V-s / U; an unknown stays in `GameSupport.unknowns` until verified.
5. **Game files never ship.** `redistributeBase: false` always; game-derived content is job-only and never enters a
   library; game binaries and decompiled code never enter git.
6. **Host seam.** New Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through `lib/cyrus/host` (`test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts`).
7. **Flag nothing on.** Registration, catalog status, settings and deploys are owner gates.
8. **One heavy job at a time** on node-2 through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost`; nothing heavy on the primary.

## Roles
| Role | Who | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | the owner only | signs the gates below; decides legal, money, flags, launch |
| Research agent | Sonnet, one pass per area | phases 0, 1, 5 (sources), 6 runs, 7 adversarial read |
| Build agent | Opus, few agents, one owner per file | phases 2, 3 (proposal), 4, 8 |
| Reviewer | a second agent | adversarial security pass, research spot-check of U labels |

Agent briefs with frugality and safety rules baked in: [templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md](templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md),
[SCREENING](templates/agent-briefs/SCREENING.md), [RESEARCH](templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md) (R1-R9, one per area),
[BUILD](templates/agent-briefs/BUILD.md) (B1-B5), [REVIEW](templates/agent-briefs/REVIEW.md) (verification run,
adversarial pass, lessons learned).

## Owner gates
| Gate | Phase | The owner signs that |

## Cross-game contract gaps (raise before building game #2)
1. `GameSupport.language` has no **JavaScript** and no multi-language / runtime-version form (FiveM; Java 21 vs 25).
2. `ARTIFACT_ROUTES` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod) is Minecraft-shaped: no "asset pack + plugin"
   (Hytale), "stream resource" (FiveM), "content mod both sides" (tModLoader), "workshop item" (Zomboid, GMod).
3. `ASSET_KINDS` has no **animation** or **material**; the AssetProfile has no sound or UI format field (only the
   catalog `audio` hint).
4. Two delivery vocabularies: `AssetDelivery.via` (server-pushed-pack / client-zip / client-mod / server-files) vs
   `AssetProfile.delivery` (server-streamed / workshop-* / client-manual). Unify them.
5. `TestLane` cannot say "needs a credential" (Hytale OAuth per server, FiveM licence key): add a credentialed lane
   flag so the owner gate is explicit.
6. `InstallRules.side` is single-valued; Valheim and tModLoader decide side per archetype.
7. Knowledge lives in two systems (Minecraft version sheets vs GameSupport knowledge packs; research G-gaps (b)).
8. The template generators (`lib/cyrus/engine/games/*`) are not referenced from the adapter; the adapter should
   name its generator / build lane.
9. The Cyrus game id and the Nxeon game family slug can differ (`zomboid` / `projectzomboid`): one mapping table.

- **Path memory** = weekly table (archetype, lanes, tier, fresh/change) -> success, kept rate, cost p25/50/90, best effort/recipe, n>=8; suggestions only; changes ship as gated engine releases.

Candidates (5 kinds) are written to a gitignored dir + `review.md`; nothing edits rules/sheets/prompts automatically; anonymised export (no request text, names, user ids, user code, imports); template sharing separate and opt-in; release manifest requires an eval gate and keeps a rollback pointer but is **not wired to deploys** (V BK). ### C5. How recipe memory and the starter bank fit (V design, nothing built)

- **Recipe** = S4 output (verified pattern for one mechanic, <=900 tokens, injected into the first user turn, cache-safe). Selection is free: the existing Haiku guard returns up to 2 archetype ids from the closed list of 85; deterministic scorer cross-checks; wrong recipe is worse than none so inject only when `status:verified` and agreement.
- **Path memory** = weekly table (archetype, lanes, tier, fresh/change) -> success, kept rate, cost p25/50/90, best effort/recipe, n>=8; suggestions only; changes ship as gated engine releases.
- **Starter bank** (B8) = curated builds of template chips, served only by allowlisted key (never the cross-user `MB_DEDUPE`); re-runs validate/precheck/javac/scan on every serve; "ready-made, instant, ~5 tokens" on plan screen.
- **NxKit** (B9) = tested helper API (Cfg/Cmd/Store/Msg) so recipes carry less skeleton; later.
- Effect (U): 15-35% per hit build, hit rate 35-55%, so 5-19% of total spend; scaffoldable boilerplate is only 26% of code (4-10% of a plain build), the real gain is fewer repair loops.

### C6. Review gate for the learning loop (V)

Candidates (5 kinds) are written to a gitignored dir + `review.md`; nothing edits rules/sheets/prompts automatically; anonymised export (no request text, names, user ids, user code, imports); template sharing separate and opt-in; release manifest requires an eval gate and keeps a rollback pointer but is **not wired to deploys** (V BK). Keep it that way: human review of every candidate, eval before release, no model fine-tuning (Claude cannot be fine-tuned by Cyrus; "learning" = rules, sheets, recipes, routing).
